# Chapter 9-i — Group G: C-9

**Document:** `NH_MASTER-21_SYSTEM_BEHAVIOR_v0_1_CANDIDATE__CH09-i.md`  
**Status:** CANDIDATE  
**Source repository:** `nesgeva/NH-GOVERNANCE`  
**Source commit:** `6a7160ba688ba4e433a31899162815df7e2bab17`  

This piece covers the access model, the complete accepted Personal Mode wiring, confirmed voice I/O and its enrollment boundary, the recorded speech-output setup, phone-control policy, restored candidate names and conversation-rehearsal constraints. Existing identity, biometric, privacy, observation and output-delivery owners retain their canonical cards. The complete model and durable-operation kernel scopes belong to CH10-b, the mobile three-mode specification to CH10-d, interface design to CH10-e, side paths to CH11 and final registers to CH12. Unspecified B29/B30 mechanisms, A21 language models, A23 rehearsal mechanics, empirical values and final implementations remain open.

V10's repeated-query and nonconsumption rule is retained, consistently with CH09-e.]

## Named review dispositions

The complete behavior was reviewed for misfiled restrictions, failure outcomes and gates, including every USED BY row. Each positive scan hit below is retained for its named reason.

| Card / line | Flag | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| C-9.1 — Recovered access model; line 116 | prerequisite_review / Gated by | Sensitive-operation re-verification is part of the recovered model, with specific owner gates in children and code-boundary failure explicit. It does not add a universal outer gate on defining the model. |
| C-9.1.4 — Authentication factor roles; line 212 | prerequisite_review / Gated by | A path requiring a factor is the factor-role rule being described. Actual owner inputs and refusal behavior are explicit; no extra universal gate on the role hierarchy is designed. |
| C-9.1.4.4 — SIA evidence role; line 308 | prerequisite_review / Gated by | Startup SIA recalculation is the required owner input and SACL handles unsafe evidence. This defines the identity-assessment factor role, not a second outer identity authority. |
| C-9.1.7 — Trusted-application access; line 470 | prerequisite_review / Gated by | Explicit authorization defines this application boundary and is stated in Does and Must never; an untrusted opening surface is refused in Fails closed. The use row imposes current opening provenance on C-9.6, whose factor/origin sequence is explicit. No separate verifier or additional outer gate is invented. |
| C-9.3.5.1 — Kill Switch immediate access termination; line 1588 | prerequisite_review / Gated by | Fresh deliberate action is required for later reconnection. It is not a gate delaying the current Kill Switch stop/disconnect. |
| C-9.3.5.2 — Kill Switch desktop stop and lock; line 1611 | prerequisite_review / Gated by | Fresh deliberate restart is required after the current stop and lock. It does not authorize continuing the present Full Mode session. |
| C-9.3.9 — Unspecified phone-control mechanics; line 1872 | prerequisite_review / Fails closed by | The prerequisite is design-level: B30 mechanical implementation remains uncompleted. Policy boundaries and the actual later owner are explicit; no runtime enforcement mechanism or new authorization gate is invented. |
| C-9.3.9 — Unspecified phone-control mechanics; line 1876 | prerequisite_review / Gated by | The prerequisite is design-level: B30 mechanical implementation remains uncompleted. Policy boundaries and the actual later owner are explicit; no runtime enforcement mechanism or new authorization gate is invented. |
| C-9.12.5.4 — Atomic SACL state reference; line 5077 | prerequisite_review / Gated by | The requirement in the use row belongs to revalidation at C-9.12.5.14. This field carries the atomic SACL reference; its owner input, mixed-read prohibition and invalidation outcome are explicit without another gate on storing the reference. |
| C-9.12.5.5 — SACL committed version reference; line 5111 | prerequisite_review / Gated by | The still-matching version requirement belongs to the using revalidation card. SACL owns the version; mismatch invalidates the snapshot. Recording the owner version does not create a new version authority. |
